For oeq:uniform-feasible-pc, replace the prose “leave-one-edge-out exact-support PC handle” by the following explicit polynomial-time construction. Put X=Z−1/2, P=widehat Pi_r(A), and C=PA. Prove uniformly over h that q_h^(1)=4AX and q_h^(2)=0, and define
  tilde gamma_{i,h}=q_{i,h}−4(CX)_i.
Project only the bandwidth-free first Hoeffding component; do not project the third-and-higher exact-support components. Define the observable residualization-bias certificate
  widehat Delta_pc =
    (2B/n) sum_i |C_ii|
    +(B/n) sum_{i:N_i>0} N_i^{-1}
       sum_{j:A_ij=1}|C_ij|.
Derive this certificate from
  |E[X_iY_i|A,f]|≤B/2,
  |E[X_jY_i|A,f]|≤B/(4N_i) for A_ij=1,
and zero covariance outside the closed neighborhood. Construct widehat V_pc from the conditional ANOVA decomposition of sum_i tilde gamma_{i,h}Y_i, using the exact residual matrix (I−P)A and explicit graph-computable norms for the third-and-higher score projections. Prove, rather than assume,
  widehat Delta_pc=O_P(d/n)=O_P(r_sup)
and
  widehat V_pc=O_P(d/n)
uniformly for C_log log n≤d=o(n). Use sparse-matrix spectral concentration for
  ||(I−P)A||_op=|lambda_{r+1}(A)|=O_P(sqrt d),
and use Abbe–Fan–Wang–Zhong Theorem 2.1/its row-and-column leave-one-out argument only to control the diagonal and edge-restricted entries of C=PA. Do not cite Li–Wager Theorem 6 for the logarithmic-degree range: its own hypothesis is rho_n polynomially larger than n^{-1/2}, and its projector lemma requires the test vector to be independent of A conditional on U. If the stated C-entry bounds fail under the frozen Bernstein eigenfunction condition, report the resulting explicit graph-norm term in widehat Delta_pc or widehat V_pc; do not add incoherence, bounded-eigenfunction, minimum-degree, or stronger sparsity assumptions.

For oeq:tail-adaptive-completion, do not attempt PC-cell imputation under the current conditional-on-(A,f) certificate. State explicitly that B sqrt(pi_0,n/n) is an unconditional testing fluctuation, not a conditional identification radius. The strongest unchanged-assumption result keeps the B pi_0 upper allowance; the strongest alternative target is the supported-unit derivative average and must be labeled as a target change.

Fix \(0\leq m\leq\lfloor d/2\rfloor\) and write
\[
 K_m(A)=\sum_{i\in\mathcal V_n}\mathbf1\{N_i\leq m\}.
\]
For every admissible \((U,A,Z)\)-marginal that remains in \(\mathcal M_{n,d,L}\) after adjoining independent Rademacher response signs, there is an explicit odd \(C^3\) degree-lattice bump whose derivative at one half has magnitude at least \(c a_m\), vanishes at every exposure lattice point of every degree at most \(m\), and yields
\[
 \inf_{\widetilde\theta}\mathbb E_P|\widetilde\theta-\theta_n|
 \geq \frac{c a_m}{n}\mathbb E_P\sqrt{K_m(A)}.
\]
Moreover,
\[
 \frac1n\mathbb E_P\sqrt{K_m(A)}
 \leq\sqrt{\frac{n^{-1}\mathbb E_PK_m(A)}{n}}
 \leq\sqrt{\frac{\pi_{m,n}}{n}}.
\]
Thus the frozen mean-mass quantity \(a_m\sqrt{\pi_{m,n}/n}\) is an upper bound on the scale certified by this missing-sign experiment, not a lower bound without an additional count-concentration argument.  For \(m=0\), the certified isolate scale is \(B n^{-1}\mathbb E_P\sqrt{K_0(A)}\).

changed.to:
Order the eigenvalues of the symmetric matrix \(A\) by decreasing absolute value, breaking equal-absolute-value ties by decreasing signed value.  Within every remaining repeated eigenspace, choose the orthonormal basis obtained by applying Gram--Schmidt to the nonzero vectors in the ordered list of projections of \(e_1,\ldots,e_n\) onto that eigenspace.  Let \(\widehat\Psi_r(A)\) contain the first \(r\) resulting orthonormal eigenvectors and define
\[

\]
This deterministic tie rule makes \(A\mapsto\widehat\Pi_r(A)\) a fixed Borel-measurable sample map.
changed.reason: A top-eigenspace prescription without a cutoff-tie rule is not a single measurable sample map.  The deterministic spectral ordering and lexicographic basis selection make the projector well defined for every observed graph.

  c_0≤kappa and b_psi≥(r−1)/sqrt(r).

Use iid random intercepts with density
  p_s(t)=s^{-1} cos^2(pi t/(2s)) 1{|t|≤s}, s=B/4,
and response pairs f_i^±(a,x)=xi_i±g(x). Record the translation inequality
  H^2(p_s(.-a),p_s(.-b))≤pi^2(a−b)^2/(4s^2),

  g_G(x)=c_G B sqrt(d/n)(x−1/2).

  E sum_i V_i^2 1{N_i>0}=O(n/d)
and nP(N_i=0)=O(n exp(−c d)).
Choose c_G small so joint TV is below a fixed constant. The target separation is order sqrt(d/n).

2. Interior bump:
fix an odd C^3 bump phi supported in (−1,1), phi(0)=0, phi'(0)=1, and define
  g_h(x)=c_I L h^3 phi((x−1/2)/h).

  P(|V_i|≤h,N_i>0)≤C sqrt(d) h

  P(max_i N_i>D_n)=o(1)
by a binomial Chernoff bound and union bound. Use a C^3 bump supported strictly inside |x−1/2|<1/(2D_n), vanishing at x=1/2, with third derivative bounded by L and center derivative of order L/D_n^2.
